statute_check: PA Municipalities Planning Code §508 (saved dl/pa_statute/mpc_full.txt, from palegis.us Act 247 of 1968 PDF): the 90-day decision clock runs from 'the regular meeting of the governing body or the planning agency (whichever first reviews the application) next following the date the application is filed'; a denial must 'specify the defects found in the application'. The full MPC text contains no 'complete application', 'completeness' or 'incomplete' (grep). No state-mandated pre-review written deficiency loop for land development plans.
disqualifier_checks: Ch. 180 SALDO (ecode360 GR2185, code current to 2025-01-06): read §180-9..18, Art V (§180-19/20), Art VI (§180-21/22), Art VII (§180-23/24) and §180-4 definitions; grep for incomplet/complete/accept/officially/deemed/filed/reject/return/'not be reviewed|considered|placed'. No completeness, acceptance or 'officially filed' clause. Contents in §180-21/23 are framed as what 'The Planning Commission may require', not as a filing condition.
§180-14B: 'No action shall be taken on any application or appeal until all application fees, charges and expenses have been paid in full.' Fee-only precondition, not a completeness check.

§180-22A begins 'Upon receipt of the required plans and application materials, the Borough Secretary shall forward ...' - read as the Secretary's distribution duty; no determination, notice or return step is attached. Residual ambiguity noted.

Application form (Rev 10-1-22), read in full: instruction 3 'All applications must be accompanied by five (5) plot plan or floor plan hard copies and one (1) electronic copy (pdf) before the application will be accepted.' This requires the plan itself and the fee (office box checks only 'Is application accompanied by plot or floor plan(s)' and fees). It is not a check of plan contents or supporting documents; practice shows plans missing utilities/stormwater/lighting entering PC review. Flag for Will: a strict reading could call copies+fee a minimal acceptance condition.

Ch. 166 Stormwater (§166-21A): 'The municipality shall require receipt of a complete plan, as specified in this chapter.' This governs the Municipal Engineer's drainage-plan consistency review (a separate stormwater approval required before LD approval), not acceptance of the land development application; the Feb 2023 minutes show an LD plan with no stormwater information heard by the PC.
§205-50 zoning site development plans: presubmission conference decides which elements to submit; Commission acts within 60 days of the meeting, failure = deemed approval; no completeness clause.

Borough web 'Permits and Zoning' page: 'Permits are issued by the Zoning Officer once it is determined that all documentation has been submitted' - applies to the Land Use/Zoning permit issued after plan approval, not to the land development plan.

Mar 14 2022 PC minutes list New Business item 'a. Accept the submission of the Buchanan Flats preliminary land development plan' - the PC 'accepts' a submission at its own meeting (PA practice for fixing the MPC filing date); that item was tabled at the developer's request with no completeness finding. Acceptance is a PC act at the formal-review meeting, not a staff hold; 19 PC minutes 2022-2025 grepped for accept/complete/returned show no plan refused or returned as incomplete.
reason: Code: plans go to the Borough Secretary, who distributes them; the PC reviews them 'at its first regular meeting following the date of submittal'; contents are what the PC 'may require'; the clock runs from filing (MPC §508); no completeness/acceptance clause in Ch. 180 or §205-50; only preconditions are the fee and the plan copies. Practice (manager-written PC minutes 2022-2023): a land development plan noted as 'incomplete and did not include information related to utilities or stormwater' was heard as New Business and tabled; a Dollar General plan was heard over three meetings without a lighting plan and tabled 'pending ... the submittal of a formal lighting plan'. Gaps come back as consultant review letters and PC tabling, i.e. inside formal review. Residual risks: the form's 'before the application will be accepted' line (plan copies + fee only) and §166-21A's 'complete plan' for the separate stormwater approval.
